variants.notes: For ordinal outcomes report the probability of superiority or rank-biserial correlation, not a Hodges-Lehmann shift on codes (DescrTab2 flag Q05). Simulation on 2026-10-03 (R 4.6.1, 4000 replicates, normal data with P(X > Y) = 0.5, n = 10 with SD 4 versus n = 30 with SD 1, alpha 0.05, normal approximation): stats::wilcox.test rejected in 12.65 % and brunnermunzel::brunnermunzel.test in 4.67 %; with the SDs swapped between the groups the rejection rates were 1.63 % and 5.45 %. Illustration only, not validation (fagerland2009).

variants.estimand_en: Equality of two independent binomial probabilities p1 = p2; p-value = min(1, 2 x smaller one-sided p), each one-sided p maximised over the common nuisance probability with the one-sided Fisher p-value as ordering statistic.

r_functions.call_sketch: inferguidR::boschloo_test(x1, n1, x2, n2, variant = "central", alpha = 0.05, groups = c("<group 1 = reference group>", "<group 2>"), event = "<event level>")  # x1 events among n1 in group 1, x2 among n2 in group 2; inferguidR's own engine (D12): relative tie tolerance 1e-7 with exact integer fallback, refined nuisance supremum with a rigorous bound
inferguidR::boschloo_power(n1, n2, p1, p2, alpha = 0.05, variant = "central")  # exact power of a fixed design, same rejection region as boschloo_test()
inferguidR::boschloo_sample_size(p1, p2, power = 0.8, alpha = 0.05, variant = "central", allocation_ratio = 1)  # same-test planning: first and stable design of the declared allocation sequence

Exact::exact.test(data = tab_2x2, method = "boschloo", tsmethod = "central", model = "Binomial", cond.row = TRUE, to.plot = FALSE)  # rows are the groups (cond.row = TRUE); alternative refers to p1 - p2 (row 1 minus row 2); matched a tie-inclusive enumeration on 426 tables on 2026-10-03; comparator only (Suggests, D12): phase 09A found agreement with inferguidR's engine within 4.6e-9 for p <= 0.5 on 17,728 tables; Exact doubles the one-sided p in the observed direction, so tables with equal sample proportions differ (specs/method-notes/boschloo.md section 2)

variants.notes: Same definition as DescrTab2's automatic Boschloo route (exact2x2 1.7.0 defaults, nPgrid = 100). Grid settings are part of the variant key; one table in the DescrTab2 audit gave a slightly smaller p at nPgrid = 100 than at 2000 (provisional). Event level and reference group are explicit inputs. A confidence interval, if shown, comes from a separately labelled procedure (DescrTab2 flag Q08). Never replaced by Fisher above a sample-size threshold (flag Q09). Observation 2026-10-03 (R 4.6.1, exact2x2 1.7.0, Exact 3.3; provisional, not validation): exact2x2::boschloo omitted sample tables whose Fisher ordering p-value ties the observed one in exact arithmetic but differs from it by about 5e-17 in floating point. Example: 1/7 vs 4/5 events, one-sided (p2 > p1): exact2x2 0.017398; enumeration including the tied table 0/7 vs 3/5 (both Fisher p = 1/22) 0.023179; Exact::exact.test 0.023179. Two-sided central: 0.034796 vs 0.046358. Over all tables of the designs 7 vs 5, 6 vs 6, 10 vs 10 and 15 vs 12 (426 tables), the exact2x2 central p was smaller than the tie-inclusive enumeration in 37 tables (by up to 0.27) and never larger; Exact 3.3 matched the enumeration in all 426; no decision at alpha = 0.05 changed in these designs. DescrTab2's automatic route inherits this behaviour. Phase 09A must use a tie-tolerant ordering (or verify by enumeration) before any template or planning engine relies on exact2x2::boschloo.

gpower_candidate.basis: G*Power has no Boschloo procedure. The June 2023 manual documents only Fisher's exact test for two independent proportions (chapter 6, a conditional test with unconditional power), and the application's unconditional procedure (exact_proportions_unconditional) orders tables by other statistics, not by the Fisher p-value; both are comparators with a different method. Classification by phase 09A (specs/method-notes/boschloo.md section 11), provisional until the procedure's options are confirmed by application captures.

inferguidR::boschloo_power(n1, n2, p1, p2, alpha = 0.05, variant = "minlike")  # exact power of a fixed design, same rejection region as boschloo_test()
inferguidR::boschloo_sample_size(p1, p2, power = 0.8, alpha = 0.05, variant = "minlike", allocation_ratio = 1)  # same-test planning: first and stable design of the declared allocation sequence

Exact::exact.test(data = tab_2x2, method = "boschloo", tsmethod = "square", model = "Binomial", cond.row = TRUE, to.plot = FALSE)  # comparator only (Suggests, D12); rows are the groups; phase 09A: inferguidR's minlike ordering corresponds to Exact tsmethod "square"

variants.notes: The exact2x2 validation vignette reports Boschloo comparisons for this option (BOSCHLOO.md). Not reachable through DescrTab2::descr() (flag Q16). In one table Exact 3.3 tsmethod 'square' gave a value close to, but not identical with, exact2x2 minlike; equivalence of the definitions is unconfirmed. Second table checked on 2026-10-03 (1/7 vs 4/5): exact2x2 minlike 0.038567, Exact 3.3 'square' 0.038574. Floating-point ties in the ordering (see boschloo_two_sided_central) were enumerated only for the central and one-sided variants, not for minlike. Phase 09A (2026-10-05): this variant corresponds to Exact 3.3 tsmethod 'square'; both agree with inferguidR's engine (for example 7/20 vs 2/22: 0.04513832; specs/method-notes/boschloo.md section 10).

r_functions.call_sketch: inferguidR::boschloo_test(x1, n1, x2, n2, variant = "less" | "greater", alpha = 0.05, groups = c("<group 1 = reference group>", "<group 2>"), event = "<event level>")  # x1 events among n1 in group 1, x2 among n2 in group 2; inferguidR's own engine (D12): relative tie tolerance 1e-7 with exact integer fallback, refined nuisance supremum with a rigorous bound; variant = "less" means H1: p1 < p2 and "greater" means H1: p1 > p2, with group 1 the explicit reference group and events counted at the explicit event level (exact2x2 alternative = "greater" corresponds to variant = "less")
inferguidR::boschloo_power(n1, n2, p1, p2, alpha = 0.05, variant = "less" | "greater")  # exact power of a fixed design, same rejection region as boschloo_test()

inferguidR::boschloo_sample_size(p1, p2, power = 0.8, alpha = 0.05, variant = "less" | "greater", allocation_ratio = 1)  # same-test planning: first and stable design of the declared allocation sequence

variants.notes: Only with a documented pre-specified direction; orientation is never taken from level order (DescrTab2 flag Q14). Direction convention checked on 2026-10-03 against the uncondExact2x2 help page ('higher values suggest larger theta2 compared to theta1') and numerically: with directions aligned as in the call sketch, the one-sided Boschloo p never exceeded the one-sided Fisher p on all tables of 7 vs 5, 6 vs 6 and 4 vs 9. Observation 2026-10-03 (R 4.6.1, exact2x2 1.7.0, Exact 3.3; provisional, not validation): exact2x2::boschloo omitted sample tables whose Fisher ordering p-value ties the observed one in exact arithmetic but differs from it by about 5e-17 in floating point. Example: 1/7 vs 4/5 events, one-sided (p2 > p1): exact2x2 0.017398; enumeration including the tied table 0/7 vs 3/5 (both Fisher p = 1/22) 0.023179; Exact::exact.test 0.023179. Two-sided central: 0.034796 vs 0.046358. Over all tables of the designs 7 vs 5, 6 vs 6, 10 vs 10 and 15 vs 12 (426 tables), the exact2x2 central p was smaller than the tie-inclusive enumeration in 37 tables (by up to 0.27) and never larger; Exact 3.3 matched the enumeration in all 426; no decision at alpha = 0.05 changed in these designs. DescrTab2's automatic route inherits this behaviour. Phase 09A must use a tie-tolerant ordering (or verify by enumeration) before any template or planning engine relies on exact2x2::boschloo. Revision 2026-10-05.1: the call sketches name inferguidR's engine; the direction statements above use exact2x2's convention (alternative = 'greater' means p2 > p1), which corresponds to inferguidR variant = 'less'.
